alternatives.root_cause: ad is cut off from the network and cannot reach its dependencies, so callers see failures.
alternatives.why_not: ad continued to serve requests with normal, short durations and its spans reached the trace store (tr_4cc23161b3d1); only the telemetry exporter host failed to resolve, and callers failed fast rather than hanging to deadlines.

alternatives.root_cause: A wrong configuration value on ad broke the GetAds path.
alternatives.why_not: The change log for ad was observed over a 24h window and held nothing (tr_bb7bcdd0be6b), so no configuration value was edited.

alternatives.root_cause: ad became slow and callers failed waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: Peak ad self-time in the sampled traces is ~15ms (tr_4cc23161b3d1), far below any plausible client deadline, so waiting is not the failing mechanism.

verdict.summary: A runtime feature flag governing the ad service's GetAds path was flipped, causing an intermittent fraction of ad requests to fail and surfacing as errors at frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: Errors appear at the edge (frontend-proxy) and at the client (load-generator) but the only in-path service whose own calls fail is ad, and the blast radius includes flagd, which sits on ad's evaluation path. The failure is a partial, intermittent error fraction (tr_99f274a85bb5, tr_b21c556a7169) rather than hangs: ad spans complete in single-digit to tens of milliseconds (tr_4cc23161b3d1, tr_e371ffb70571), which rules out process_freeze, network_partition and dependency_latency as the mechanism seen by callers. Change logs for both ad and flagd were observed and are empty (tr_bb7bcdd0be6b, tr_6c93c8ed2f2f), so no artifact or config file changed, which is exactly the signature of a flag store flip. ad continues to serve and log request handling; the only exception text in its log concerns its telemetry exporter's name resolution (tr_87fa092d3410), which affects export rather than the GetAds request path and does not explain caller-visible errors. Other services in the same traces (product-catalog, cart, recommendation, product-reviews) are healthy, so this is not infrastructure-wide.
open_questions: No flagd log lines were returned for the window (tr_9a693f1443a6), so the specific flag name, its new value and the exact flip time were not observed.
frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator produced no log lines (tr_134dcc12ae87, tr_6e880136f836, tr_5092a891702e), so the status codes callers actually received were not directly confirmed.
The DNS failure to the telemetry collector seen in ad's log is unexplained and may indicate a separate, concurrent environment problem affecting observability completeness.
